_comment: Third-person movement tuning. ALL of it is TUNABLE and none of it is a mechanic. These are starting values chosen to be playable, not balanced; the owner's job in M1 is to say 'too floaty', 'sprint too slow', 'camera too close', and these are the numbers that answer that. Nothing here should be treated as settled until traversal feels good on the Ally.

locomotion._comment_accel: Metres per second squared. Ground acceleration high enough that the character does not feel like it is on ice, air acceleration low enough that mid-jump direction changes read as momentum rather than flight.
locomotion._comment_turn: How fast the character model swings to face travel direction, radians/sec. Too low reads as sluggish, too high reads as a turret.

gait_feel._comment: MQ1A, TUNABLE. Momentum tilt: the trainer's model leans into acceleration and banks into turns (character_model.gd::apply_momentum_tilt, driven from trainer_model.gd). lean_deg_per_accel converts m/s^2 to degrees; at ground_acceleration 42 the launch lean approaches pitch_limit_deg. smoothing_rate is 1/seconds-to-settle-ish; higher snaps, lower wallows.

jump._comment: Height in metres, converted to launch velocity against gravity so retuning gravity does not silently change jump height.
jump._comment_gravity: Well above real 9.8. Realistic gravity in a third-person game reads as floating; this is the single biggest lever on 'too floaty' feedback.
jump._comment_fall_mult: Falling accelerates faster than rising. Standard platformer trick that makes a jump feel weighty without shortening its rise.
jump._comment_forgiveness: Coyote time lets a jump register just after walking off an edge; buffer lets a jump pressed just before landing fire on touchdown. Both are invisible when they work and infuriating when absent.

stamina._comment_delay: Seconds after the last stamina spend before regeneration starts. Without a delay, tapping sprint costs nothing and the meter is decoration.
stamina._comment_exhausted: Below this, sprint is refused until the meter recovers past it. Stops a stutter-sprint exploit at 1 stamina.

fall_damage._comment: Damage is driven by impact SPEED, not by fall distance: the same landing hurts the same whether it came off a cliff or a launch. safe_speed is roughly a 2.5m drop under the gravity above.
fall_damage._comment_curve: Exponent on the normalised speed between safe and lethal. Above 1 makes small overshoots cheap and big ones brutal, which is what makes a player judge a drop rather than avoid all of them.

camera._comment: Orbit camera on a spring arm. distance/height are the resting pose; the arm shortens automatically when terrain intrudes.
camera._comment_pitch: Degrees. Negative looks down. The lower bound stops the camera going under the terrain, the upper stops it looking at the sky behind the player's head.
camera._comment_sensitivity: Gamepad is degrees/second at full stick. Mouse is degrees per pixel of motion. They are separate numbers because tuning one to fix the other always makes the other worse.
camera._comment_deadzone: The Ally's sticks rest slightly off centre and drift with wear. Applied on top of the input map's own deadzone.
camera._comment_follow: How quickly the arm's origin catches up to the player, and how quickly it recovers after terrain pushes it in. Collision recovery is deliberately slower than intrusion, so the camera snaps away from a wall but eases back out.
camera._comment_collision_margin: How far the spring arm stops short of whatever it hit. The Meadows scatter's trees and rocks collide (scripts/world/vegetation.gd), and are dense enough that a trunk can sit almost directly behind the player; the old 0.3 default then read as the camera buried in bark rather than a normal close-up.

torch._comment: Owner playtest report: night is too dark, and the player needs a torch from the beginning rather than discovering that in the dark and only then being able to craft one. There is no torch ITEM to craft or lose -- it is a fixed part of the trainer's kit from the first frame, same as the belt. `auto_at_night` means it needs no input at all to satisfy 'available immediately': it lights itself the moment world_look.gd's is_dark() goes true, and torch_toggle (L / gamepad Start) is a manual OVERRIDE on top of that, not the only way to turn it on.
torch._comment_placement: Metres above the player's feet, and forward -- roughly chest height, angled down and out so it reads as a carried light illuminating the ground ahead rather than a beacon strapped to the forehead.
torch._comment_light: Warm (low colour temperature) on purpose -- a cool-white spotlight reads as a flashlight/sci-fi prop, not a torch. Range and angle are tuned to light the ground and nearby foliage a few paces out without turning night into day; energy is kept modest for the same reason and because a single shadow-casting light following the player at all times is the wrong place to spend the handheld's frame budget.
